sources.title: Wasmtime security model, pinned source
sources.version: Wasmtime v49.0.2 tag; commit 3c8a3e7 (verified by release page)

sources.observed_operation: Opened official repository file at the v49.0.2 tag and read the sandbox/interface/defense-in-depth sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guest I/O is through explicitly linked imports; WASI filesystem access is capability-oriented. Runtime implementation bugs can still undermine the sandbox; defense-in-depth controls are not proofs of absence of escape.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit host APIs and an additional process boundary; does not certify the proposed host embedding.

sources.title: Wasmtime execution interruption settings, pinned source
sources.locator: consume_fuel, epoch_interruption, and interaction with blocking host calls
sources.observed_operation: Opened source and located fuel/epoch configuration documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fuel is disabled by default and must be supplied to each Store. Epochs are nondeterministic. Fuel/epochs do not time out guest code blocked in a host call; embedder must make the host operation cancellable/bounded.
sources.applicability: Directly informs responsiveness budgets for a Wasmtime execution path.

reviser_recheck.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:57Z–00:59Z; web reader exposes page retrieval but not per-request seconds
reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged source and located the blocking-host-call comments with a targeted text lookup.
reviser_recheck.governing_condition_default_exception: Neither fuel nor epoch interruption wakes or times out guest code blocked in a host call; the embedder must bound and cancel host work. Async host calls can yield to an event loop for timeout/cancellation.
reviser_recheck.applicability: Supports CT-01 correction: every host import needs its own bounded, cancellable operation, with cancellation propagated to the supervisor.

sources.title: Wasmtime resource limiter implementation, pinned source
sources.locator: ResourceLimiter caveat and StoreLimitsBuilder defaults
sources.observed_operation: Opened official tagged Rust implementation and located resource limiter docs/defaults.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limiter caps instance resources; it does not account for all Store/runtime or embedder-specific host allocations. StoreLimitsBuilder memory/table caps default to unlimited; instance/table/memory count defaults are 10,000.
sources.applicability: Requires explicit caps plus host allocation quotas and/or OS process limits.

sources.observed_operation: Opened official release page; read tag/commit and security-fix list.

sources.title: Wasmtime WASI poll_oneoff fuel bypass advisory
sources.locator: Affected versions, impact, affected embeddings, patches
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Wasmtime security advisory and read exact affected conditions and patch versions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WASI Preview 0 poll_oneoff performed O(n) host work without fuel check; library embeddings affected only when Preview 0 was explicitly enabled, while CLI enabled it by default. Preview 1/2/3 were stated unaffected.
sources.applicability: Proves quotas must cover host calls and use patched runtime plus only required WASI interfaces.

sources.title: Wasmtime unbounded host allocation advisory
sources.locator: Impact, affected embeddings, patches
sources.observed_operation: Opened official advisory and checked stream/default conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WASIp2 SinkOutputStream without configured stdout/stderr allowed an unbounded host allocation; configured streams typically applied limits. Fixed in listed patch releases.
sources.applicability: Host-side memory must be bounded even if guest linear memory is limited.

sources.title: Bubblewrap design, limits and invocation model
sources.locator: Sandbox security, namespace features, limitations, lines 205-269
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged README and read sandbox construction and limitation sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bubblewrap is a low-level sandbox constructor, not a ready policy. Protection depends on arguments; every mount adds risk; D-Bus can enable host actions; TIOCSTI requires --new-session or seccomp filtering.
sources.applicability: Policy generation, mount allowlist, bus exclusion, session isolation, and strict launch failure belong to the host.

reviser_recheck.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:57Z–00:59Z; web reader exposes page retrieval but not per-request seconds

reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Opened the tagged README and inspected its boundary, namespace, mount, D-Bus, and TIOCSTI passages.
reviser_recheck.governing_condition_default_exception: The invoking arguments determine the protection; mounts and exposed D-Bus matter; network namespaces provide loopback only; TIOCSTI needs seccomp filtering or --new-session. The README does not set temporary-storage quotas.
reviser_recheck.applicability: Supports treating bubblewrap as policy construction and testing; it does not itself establish the proposed temporary storage limit.

sources.title: Flatpak user namespace requirements
sources.locator: Unprivileged bubblewrap requirements and setuid fallback tradeoff
sources.observed_operation: Read official project wiki for kernel/sysctl prerequisites and fallback.

sources.applicability: Treat as a compatibility signal only; feature-probe actual supported systems and do not silently weaken policy.

sources.title: Linux cgroup v2 resource controls
sources.version: Latest kernel documentation as observed 2026-10-12; not release-pinned
sources.locator: Limits and memory.max sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened official kernel docs and read cgroup limit semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits default to max/no-op unless configured. memory.max is hard limit but may briefly be exceeded; control requires host-managed cgroup access.
sources.applicability: Linux CPU/memory/pids controls need a manager/delegation and failure tests; bubblewrap alone does not establish these budgets.

sources.title: Windows AppContainer isolation
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 docs, no specific API release tag
sources.locator: File, network, process isolation sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn and read AppContainer isolation categories.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filesystem/network access can be granted narrowly; process/kernel object isolation prevents cross-process influence when properly contained. The page notes some resources may be available by default and brokers may mediate others.
sources.applicability: Windows native worker candidate; maintain minimal capability grants and validate default resources on supported Windows versions.

reviser_recheck.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:57Z–00:59Z; web reader exposes page retrieval but not per-request seconds

sources.title: Launching AppContainer or LPAC process
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 docs; AppContainer introduced with Windows 8 per page
sources.locator: Capability SIDs and launching via STARTUPINFOEX/attribute list
sources.observed_operation: Opened launch guide and read process-start steps.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateProcess startup attributes must include AppContainer attributes; capabilities are explicit. Regular AppContainer has some base resources; LPAC is narrower but requires more explicit grants.
sources.applicability: Real native launch integration work; validate the exact package/unpackaged setup rather than assume process creation applies a sandbox.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects process and resource management
sources.locator: Kill-on-job-close and managing a process tree sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn and read process-tree/termination constraints.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates associated processes; allowing breakaway can leave children untracked. Nested jobs are supported beginning Windows 8, with older-version caveats.
sources.applicability: Use a killable job, avoid breakaway, set resource limits, and test child process behavior in addition to AppContainer.

reviser_recheck.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:57Z–00:59Z; web reader exposes page retrieval but not per-request seconds

reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn and used targeted lookups for Win32_Process.Create, last-handle termination, and nested/breakaway behavior.

reviser_recheck.applicability: Supports CT-03 conditions on launch, process tracking, handle control, explicit cancellation, and supported Windows versions.

sources.title: Windows file picker versus library capabilities
sources.locator: Music/Pictures/Videos/Documents and picker guidance around lines 69-84 and 249-255

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Library capabilities permit programmatic broad access; docs recommend a picker when the user can select files/folders. A selected location can be remembered through FutureAccessList if the app chooses.
sources.applicability: Use host picker and one-operation read grant; do not ask for broad library access for optional file input.

sources.title: JSON-RPC 2.0 specification
sources.locator: Notifications, error responses, batch semantics
sources.observed_operation: Opened official protocol specification and read notifications and batch sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Notifications have no response/error delivery; batches may be processed concurrently and responses can be out of order. Transport is agnostic and framing must be defined separately.
sources.applicability: Require request/response for transformations; avoid batching until ordering/idempotency semantics are specified.

sources.title: Firefox permission and update UX precedent

sources.observed_operation: Opened Mozilla extension developer guidance and read runtime/update permission pattern.

sources.applicability: UX precedent only; not a native desktop security control or guarantee.

sources.title: Windows Job Object basic limits
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 API documentation; no specific API release tag
sources.locator: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION fields and LimitFlags: per-process/per-job user time, active process count, breakaway behavior, kill-on-job-close, and related limits
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn structure reference and read its limit fields and flag descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits are configured through the job object; kill-on-job-close is a configured flag, and breakaway flags alter whether child processes remain associated. Windows-version support can differ by individual limit.
sources.applicability: Configure and test the actual job policy for the supported Windows versions; do not assume process-tree termination or quotas from merely creating a job.

sources.title: Windows Job Object extended limits and memory accounting
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 API documentation; no specific API release tag
sources.locator: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION ProcessMemoryLimit, JobMemoryLimit, and peak memory fields
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn structure reference and read process/job memory limit and peak-accounting fields.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Memory limits are explicit job settings; the structure documents configured process/job commit limits and peak accounting, not a default quota.
sources.applicability: Use explicit memory limits and verify their behavior under the deployed Windows version and launch sequence.

sources.title: Wasmtime security guide
sources.locator: WebAssembly Core and Defense-in-depth, especially checked linear memory and imports; Filesystem Access; lines 197-220
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged source page and read its sandbox model, host-interface boundary, defense-in-depth, and filesystem-access sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WebAssembly modules access the outside world through explicitly linked imports; Wasmtime describes memory isolation and mitigations. These are implementation design claims and do not establish immunity from runtime or embedder defects.
sources.applicability: Supports treating in-process Wasmtime as a distinct comparator while keeping runtime/host-call defects and shared-process resource failure in the comparison.

sources.title: Wasmtime Config fuel and epoch controls
sources.locator: Config::consume_fuel and epoch-based interruption; fuel defaults to false; a Store must receive fuel
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged implementation and read the fuel and epoch-interruption configuration comments.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fuel instrumentation is disabled by default and requires Store fuel; epochs are nondeterministic and require embedder configuration. These controls concern Wasm execution and do not by themselves bound host calls or all process resources.
sources.applicability: Supports comparing execution control and host integration burden for an embedded Wasmtime option.

sources.title: Bubblewrap README
sources.locator: Sandbox security, namespaces, and limitations; lines 205-268
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged README and read the policy-construction, namespace, mount, D-Bus, and TIOCSTI sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bubblewrap is a low-level sandbox constructor, not a ready policy; its protection depends on caller-supplied arguments and mounted resources. Network namespaces provide loopback only; TIOCSTI requires filtering or a new session.
sources.applicability: Confirms the investigator's Linux alternative is a host policy implementation with explicit integration and support burden, not a plug-and-play boundary.

sources.title: JSON-RPC 2.0 specification
sources.locator: Request IDs and response correlation; Notification behavior, sections 4–5
sources.observed_operation: Opened the protocol specification and read request ID, notification, and response requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: An omitted request ID defines a notification; notifications must receive no response and are not confirmable, so client-side error awareness is absent. Request/response calls require a response correlated by ID.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit comparison of error-reporting semantics for a serialized extension protocol.

sources.title: Tmpfs — Linux kernel documentation
sources.version: Latest Linux kernel tmpfs documentation as accessed 2026-10-12; page updated 2024-08-23; not release-pinned
sources.locator: Sizing options lines 32–42; size, nr_inodes, default sizing, and swap behavior

sources.locator: Sandbox security, namespace features, limitations, lines 205-269
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged README and read sandbox construction and limitation sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bubblewrap is a low-level sandbox constructor, not a ready policy. Protection depends on arguments; every mount adds risk; D-Bus can enable host actions; TIOCSTI requires --new-session or seccomp filtering.
sources.applicability: Policy generation, mount allowlist, bus exclusion, session isolation, and strict launch failure belong to the host.

sources.title: Bubblewrap security tests
sources.locator: No network and unreadable file tests around test-run.sh lines 1698-1734
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged test suite and read tests for network namespace and /etc/shadow denial.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tests call --unshare-net and test access denial; some setup paths can skip or vary with test environment. They were not executed in this task.
sources.applicability: Useful host integration test patterns; not evidence this proposal is already validated.

sources.title: Flatpak bubblewrap caller source
sources.version: main branch at observed access; mutable commit not surfaced
sources.locator: Caller condition adding --unshare-net when shared-network permission is absent
sources.observed_operation: Opened current Flatpak caller source and read the policy-to-argument branch.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: No network sharing adds --unshare-net; allowing devices or resources has other explicit branches. This caller demonstrates policy is constructed by a higher-level host.
sources.applicability: Supports separate policy compiler as product responsibility; branch snapshot is not a pinned release.

sources.title: Flatpak user namespace requirements
sources.locator: Unprivileged bubblewrap requirements and setuid fallback tradeoff
sources.observed_operation: Read official project wiki for kernel/sysctl prerequisites and fallback.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Unprivileged mode requires user namespaces and sufficient namespace sysctls; fallback setuid mode is not recommended and is a security tradeoff. Listed distro examples are dated.
sources.applicability: Treat as a compatibility signal only; feature-probe actual supported systems and do not silently weaken policy.

sources.title: Linux cgroup v2 resource controls
sources.version: Latest kernel documentation as observed 2026-10-12; not release-pinned
sources.locator: Limits and memory.max sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened official kernel docs and read cgroup limit semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits default to max/no-op unless configured. memory.max is hard limit but may briefly be exceeded; control requires host-managed cgroup access.
sources.applicability: Linux CPU/memory/pids controls need a manager/delegation and failure tests; bubblewrap alone does not establish these budgets.

sources.title: Windows AppContainer isolation
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 docs, no specific API release tag
sources.locator: File, network, process isolation sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn and read AppContainer isolation categories.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filesystem/network access can be granted narrowly; process/kernel object isolation prevents cross-process influence when properly contained. The page notes some resources may be available by default and brokers may mediate others.
sources.applicability: Windows native worker candidate; maintain minimal capability grants and validate default resources on supported Windows versions.

sources.title: Launching AppContainer or LPAC process
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 docs; AppContainer introduced with Windows 8 per page
sources.locator: Capability SIDs and launching via STARTUPINFOEX/attribute list
sources.observed_operation: Opened launch guide and read process-start steps.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateProcess startup attributes must include AppContainer attributes; capabilities are explicit. Regular AppContainer has some base resources; LPAC is narrower but requires more explicit grants.
sources.applicability: Real native launch integration work; validate the exact package/unpackaged setup rather than assume process creation applies a sandbox.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects process and resource management
sources.locator: Kill-on-job-close and managing a process tree sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn and read process-tree/termination constraints.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates associated processes; allowing breakaway can leave children untracked. Nested jobs are supported beginning Windows 8, with older-version caveats.
sources.applicability: Use a killable job, avoid breakaway, set resource limits, and test child process behavior in addition to AppContainer.

sources.title: Windows file picker versus library capabilities
sources.locator: Music/Pictures/Videos/Documents and picker guidance around lines 69-84 and 249-255
sources.observed_operation: Opened capability declaration table and file-picker guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Library capabilities permit programmatic broad access; docs recommend a picker when the user can select files/folders. A selected location can be remembered through FutureAccessList if the app chooses.
sources.applicability: Use host picker and one-operation read grant; do not ask for broad library access for optional file input.

sources.title: XDG FileChooser portal
sources.locator: OpenFile, filters, selected URI/result
sources.observed_operation: Opened portal interface specification and read user dialog, filters, and result semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Portal presents a chooser and selected files become accessible; filters are only a usability aid and backend may allow files outside filters. Document access may persist across sessions.
sources.applicability: Use host-controlled picker/broker; treat filters as hints, not enforcement.

sources.title: XDG Documents portal
sources.locator: Add/AddFull persistent flag and Grant/RevokePermissions
sources.observed_operation: Opened portal interface page and read document permissions and persistence methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Document exports can have per-app read/write permissions and may be persistent; Add accepts an open fd and explicit persistent flag. Version 5 also exposes host paths to authorized readers.
sources.applicability: For a single operation prefer nonpersistent export or pass bytes through the host, and avoid exposing host paths.

sources.title: JSON-RPC 2.0 specification
sources.locator: Notifications, error responses, batch semantics
sources.observed_operation: Opened official protocol specification and read notifications and batch sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Notifications have no response/error delivery; batches may be processed concurrently and responses can be out of order. Transport is agnostic and framing must be defined separately.
sources.applicability: Require request/response for transformations; avoid batching until ordering/idempotency semantics are specified.

sources.title: Firefox permission and update UX precedent
sources.version: Mozilla Extension Workshop page, observed current; page last updated 2021-03-19
sources.locator: Install/update permission prompts, optional runtime permissions, denial fallback
sources.observed_operation: Opened Mozilla extension developer guidance and read runtime/update permission pattern.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Firefox prompts when updates add permissions; declining leaves old version installed. Optional permissions can be requested at a user action and denied features should degrade gracefully.
sources.applicability: UX precedent only; not a native desktop security control or guarantee.

sources.title: Windows Job Object basic limits
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 API documentation; no specific API release tag
sources.locator: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION fields and LimitFlags: per-process/per-job user time, active process count, breakaway behavior, kill-on-job-close, and related limits
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn structure reference and read its limit fields and flag descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits are configured through the job object; kill-on-job-close is a configured flag, and breakaway flags alter whether child processes remain associated. Windows-version support can differ by individual limit.
sources.applicability: Configure and test the actual job policy for the supported Windows versions; do not assume process-tree termination or quotas from merely creating a job.

sources.title: Windows Job Object extended limits and memory accounting
sources.version: Current Microsoft Win32 API documentation; no specific API release tag
sources.locator: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION ProcessMemoryLimit, JobMemoryLimit, and peak memory fields
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn structure reference and read process/job memory limit and peak-accounting fields.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Memory limits are explicit job settings; the structure documents configured process/job commit limits and peak accounting, not a default quota.
sources.applicability: Use explicit memory limits and verify their behavior under the deployed Windows version and launch sequence.

sources.title: Wasmtime security guide
sources.locator: WebAssembly Core and Defense-in-depth, especially checked linear memory and imports; Filesystem Access; lines 197-220
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged source page and read its sandbox model, host-interface boundary, defense-in-depth, and filesystem-access sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WebAssembly modules access the outside world through explicitly linked imports; Wasmtime describes memory isolation and mitigations. These are implementation design claims and do not establish immunity from runtime or embedder defects.
sources.applicability: Supports treating in-process Wasmtime as a distinct comparator while keeping runtime/host-call defects and shared-process resource failure in the comparison.

sources.title: Wasmtime Config fuel and epoch controls
sources.locator: Config::consume_fuel and epoch-based interruption; fuel defaults to false; a Store must receive fuel
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged implementation and read the fuel and epoch-interruption configuration comments.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fuel instrumentation is disabled by default and requires Store fuel; epochs are nondeterministic and require embedder configuration. These controls concern Wasm execution and do not by themselves bound host calls or all process resources.
sources.applicability: Supports comparing execution control and host integration burden for an embedded Wasmtime option.

sources.title: Bubblewrap README
sources.locator: Sandbox security, namespaces, and limitations; lines 205-268
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tagged README and read the policy-construction, namespace, mount, D-Bus, and TIOCSTI sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bubblewrap is a low-level sandbox constructor, not a ready policy; its protection depends on caller-supplied arguments and mounted resources. Network namespaces provide loopback only; TIOCSTI requires filtering or a new session.
sources.applicability: Confirms the investigator's Linux alternative is a host policy implementation with explicit integration and support burden, not a plug-and-play boundary.

sources.title: JSON-RPC 2.0 specification
sources.locator: Request IDs and response correlation; Notification behavior, sections 4–5
sources.observed_operation: Opened the protocol specification and read request ID, notification, and response requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: An omitted request ID defines a notification; notifications must receive no response and are not confirmable, so client-side error awareness is absent. Request/response calls require a response correlated by ID.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit comparison of error-reporting semantics for a serialized extension protocol.

sources.title: WIT reference, WebAssembly Component Model
sources.version: Current official Component Model documentation as accessed 2026-10-12; page/commit not release-pinned
sources.locator: User-defined records, variants, resources; typed interfaces and handles
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official Component Model reference and read its type/resource descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WIT provides typed declarations and resource handles; domain behavior, validation invariants, and host authorization still have to be defined by the application.
sources.applicability: Supports the typed component-interface exchange option and the need to compare it with serialized IPC and shared memory.

map.purpose: Independent primary-source notes supporting critique.md. Stable source IDs retain the investigator package's existing meanings.

sources.title: Wasmtime v49.0.2 configuration and interruption comments
sources.version: Wasmtime v49.0.2 tag; investigator source map identifies commit 3c8a3e7
sources.locator: Interaction with blocking host calls, lines 3488–3503
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tagged source file and inspected the blocking-host-call comment with a targeted text lookup.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Epochs and fuel affect running WebAssembly code but do not wake or time out code blocked in a host call; embedder must bound and wake such host work.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit host-call cancellation in addition to guest fuel/epoch controls.

sources.title: Wasmtime v49.0.2 resource limiter implementation
sources.version: Wasmtime v49.0.2 tag; investigator source map identifies commit 3c8a3e7
sources.locator: ResourceLimiter allocation caveat, lines 1037–1045
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tagged source file and inspected the resource-limiter caveat with a targeted text lookup.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The limiter constrains resources allocated by a WebAssembly instance, not every Store allocation or embedder-specific allocation.
sources.applicability: Supports complementary host allocation and process-level resource limits.

sources.title: Wasmtime v49.0.2 release notes
sources.locator: Fixed items, lines 173–196
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tagged release and inspected its fixed-item list.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The notes list a WASI Preview 0 poll_oneoff fuel bypass, excessive host allocation when guests lack stdio, and a component async-lifted callback result-count validation issue causing native stack buffer overflow, among other fixes.
sources.applicability: Confirms the draft's examples of maintenance-sensitive runtime issues; fixes do not certify a host embedding.

sources.title: Bubblewrap v0.13.0 README
sources.version: v0.13.0 tag; investigator source map identifies commit 719a4fd
sources.locator: Sandbox argument responsibility, namespaces, seccomp, and limitations, lines 208–268
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tagged README and inspected the sandboxing and limitations sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Protection is determined by the invoking framework's arguments; mounts and exposed D-Bus matter; seccomp can restrict syscalls; without TIOCSTI filtering, --new-session is needed.
sources.applicability: Supports requiring a host-owned policy builder and tests; the README does not itself define a quota for temporary storage.

sources.title: Microsoft AppContainer isolation
sources.version: Current Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation; page says last updated 2025-07-08
sources.locator: File isolation and process isolation, lines 39–47; device exceptions, line 38
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn documentation and read file, process, and device isolation statements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Read-write access may be granted narrowly; read-only access is less restricted; each AppContainer can access its own memory-resident files; keyboard/mouse are listed among resources always available to AppContainer and resident application.
sources.applicability: Supports AppContainer as a meaningful boundary but requires exact-mode negative tests and qualified claims about zero filesystem/device access.

sources.title: Microsoft Job Objects
sources.version: Current Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation; page says last updated 2025-07-14
sources.locator: Child process association, termination, and tree management, lines 42–55 and 86–95
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn documentation and read process association, termination, and breakaway rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateProcess children normally join the job, but Win32_Process.Create children do not by default; breakaway flags alter association; KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE acts when the last job handle closes; job nesting varies by Windows version.
sources.applicability: Supports Job Objects for resource and lifecycle controls only when launch paths, handle inheritance, nesting, and breakaway are configured and validated.

sources.title: XDG Desktop Portal FileChooser
sources.version: FileChooser interface version 4 per investigator source map
sources.locator: OpenFile filters, lines 143–153
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official portal page and read filter semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filters aid user selection; the portal may still allow files that do not match them and applications must handle that.
sources.applicability: Supports treating file-picker filters as usability only, not an access-control test.

sources.title: XDG Desktop Portal Documents
sources.version: Documents interface version 5, stated by the page
sources.locator: Sandboxed file view and persistence flag, lines 94–102 and 125–150
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official portal page and read the sandbox filesystem view and Add() persistence semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Exported files are exposed through a restricted sandbox filesystem; Add() takes an open fd and a persistent boolean that selects session-only or permanent access.
sources.applicability: Supports one-run, host-mediated bytes or nonpersistent document grants; do not infer chooser selection alone makes a grant ephemeral.
